sections.title: This week's likely biggest movers
sections.markdown:

*Updated the evening of Oct 28, after the Fed and the after-hours reports. After-hours prices are thin and can reverse by the open. This is research, not financial advice; I'm not a licensed advisor, and the buy/sell decision is yours.*

| Stock | Sector | Why it should move most | Upside trigger | Downside trigger |

| GOOGL | AI cloud | Down \~8–10% after hours (implied ±6.1%): EPS $2.12 vs. \~$3.02 expected, free cash flow −$9.1B, 2027 capex to "rise significantly" | Buyers refocus on Cloud +103% and a $561B backlog | Cash-burn fear spreads to the other hyperscalers |

| CRWV, NBIS, ORCL | AI cloud (neoclouds) | Up 7–11% on Oct 28 after Oracle's investor day, but the most rate-sensitive names with the 10-year near 5.04% and a December hike \~83–85% priced | Yields ease, Amazon confirms demand | Hike odds and bond yields climb |

sections.title: Macro backdrop: a hawkish hold, 5% yields and $100+ oil
sections.markdown:
The Fed held, but two votes for a hike keep a December 9 increase the market's base case, which keeps pressure on high-multiple and debt-funded AI stocks.

- Fed: held at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook (her first dissent) and Cleveland's Beth Hammack wanted a 25 bp hike. The statement said "the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine" the stance and called uncertainty elevated. Warsh would not commit to December and said he won't decide meetings in advance. Futures price roughly 83–85% odds of a December hike. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html), [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/fed-chair-warsh-hesitates-on-december-rate-hike-amid-rising-treasury-yields), [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours))
- Inflation: September CPI rose 3.7% (core 2.6%), up from 3.4% in August. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html))
- Rates: the 10-year rose about 5 bp to \~5.04% during the press conference while the 2-year fell to 4.70%. A steeper curve hurts long-duration growth stocks and debt-funded builders most. ([SRN News](https://srnnews.com/fomc-holds-rates-steady-markets-rise-modestly/))
- Stocks: the S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,743.98 and the chip index (SOX) 1.8%, its fourth straight gain. Utilities and real estate lagged on higher long yields. After hours, QQQ slipped \~0.5% on Alphabet. ([TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours), [RiskReversal](https://riskreversal.substack.com/p/fed-holds-msft-higher-googl-lower))
- Oil: Brent near $111 and WTI near $101. Iran's reply to Qatar's new draft deal is expected by week's end. ([investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/investinglive-european-fx-news-wrap-28-oct/))
- AI financing: Alphabet's free cash flow was negative for a second straight quarter (−$9.1B). It raised $12.4B from share sales and $28.7B in debt during the quarter. ([Cautious Optimism](https://www.cautiousoptimism.news/msft-alpha-earnings), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/10/28/alphabet-google-stock-drops-cloud-revenue-doubles-free-cash-flow-negative))

sections.title: Options timing: are earnings options cheap or expensive?
sections.markdown:
Tonight split three ways: Microsoft moved about as much as options priced, while Alphabet and ServiceNow both moved well beyond their implied moves, to the downside. Buying calls or puts into a report only pays if the stock moves more than options already price in. Implied moves for upcoming reports are as of Oct 27–28 and will shift.

| Stock | Report | Implied move | Actual (after hours) or avg. last 5 (close) | Beat implied, last 5 (close) | Read |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MSFT | Oct 28 (done) | ±4.7%–5.3% | +2% to +6% after hours, \~+4% late | 3 of 5 before tonight | Roughly as priced |
| GOOGL | Oct 28 (done) | ±6.1% | −8% to −10.4% after hours | 2 of 5 before tonight | Beat implied; options that looked rich still underpriced the move |
| NOW | Oct 28 (done) | ±10.4% | −14% to −16% after hours | — | Beat implied, to the downside |
| AMZN | Oct 29, after close | ±7.6% | ±7.9% | 3 of 5 | Fairly priced; AWS and cash flow decide |
| INTC | Oct 29, after close | ±9.4% | ±11.5% | 3 of 5 | Cheap on average, driven by two huge moves (+23.6%, −17.0%) |
| AAPL | Nov 2, after close | ±4.4% | ±2.8% | 1 of 5 | Rich vs. recent moves; one −7.4% miss in July |
| PLTR | Nov 2, after close | ±12.0% | ±11.8% | 1 of 5 | Fairly priced; one +29.5% outlier in August |
| AMD | Nov 3, after close | ±9.3% | ±10.4% | 2 of 5 | Slightly cheap on average; two big moves (+18.6%, −17.3%) |
**What this means for timing:**

1. After hours is not the close. Tonight's moves can widen or reverse at Thursday's open; the averages above use closing moves.
2. Tonight's lesson: Alphabet's options looked rich on history and still underpriced the move. A surprise in cash flow or guidance can overwhelm the averages, so history is a base rate, not a forecast.
3. Fair or rich options (AAPL, AMZN, PLTR): buying calls or puts outright before the report has had poor odds. Debit spreads cut the cost; waiting until after the report avoids the volatility crush but misses the gap.
4. Cheaper options (INTC, AMD): moves have beaten the implied move more often, but on five reports and one or two outliers each.
5. Read-through stocks (MU, SKHY, AVGO, VRT, CRWV, NBIS): no earnings premium of their own to collapse, so a hyperscaler report reprices them overnight. Amazon tomorrow is the next such event.
6. Expiries: the first weekly after a report (Oct 30 for AMZN and INTC, Nov 6 for AAPL, PLTR and AMD) is cheapest but takes the full crush. One more week adds cushion.

Past moves don't predict the next one. Sources: [EarningsWatcher MSFT](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/msft-earnings-october-2026), [EarningsWatcher GOOGL](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/googl-earnings-october-2026), [EarningsWatcher AMZN](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/amzn-implied-move), [EarningsWatcher AMZN options](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/amzn-earnings-options), [EarningsWatcher INTC](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/intc-earnings-october-2026), [EarningsWatcher AAPL](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/aapl-implied-move), [EarningsWatcher PLTR](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/pltr-earnings-november-2026), [EarningsWatcher AMD](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/amd-earnings-november-2026), [Q3 implied vs. actual tracker](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/q3-2026-implied-vs-actual-tracker), [ZeroHedge (MSFT after hours)](https://zerohedge.com/markets/msft-rises-azure-beat-bookings-shrink-and-backlog-stalls), [RiskReversal](https://riskreversal.substack.com/p/fed-holds-msft-higher-googl-lower), [Investing.com (GOOGL)](https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/earnings-call-transcript-alphabet-q3-2026-profit-miss-sparks-10-afterhours-drop-93CH-5662008), [PANews (NOW)](https://panews.io/articles/01a1844b-23c0-762e-84fc-a5ee2a94208b), [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours).

sections.title: AI cloud
sections.markdown:
Tonight split the group: Microsoft grew Azure 48% while spending less than expected and rose; Alphabet doubled Cloud revenue but burned cash and fell. The market is paying for cloud growth and punishing negative free cash flow.

| Company | Result or setup | Versus the bar | Read |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Microsoft (MSFT)](https://phemex.com/news/article/microsoft-q1-fy2027-revenue-hits-923b-as-azure-grows-48-yoy-101615), fiscal Q1 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) | Revenue $92.3B (+19%), EPS $4.89; Azure +48% cc vs. 44–45% guide; Microsoft Cloud $63.9B (+30%) | Capex incl. leases $45.2B vs. \~$50B+ expected; commercial bookings −12%; RPO flat at $677B; FQ2 Azure guide reported at \~49% | Up \~2–6% after hours; slower spending is a mild negative for suppliers |
| [Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://fortune.com/2026/10/28/alphabet-google-stock-drops-cloud-revenue-doubles-free-cash-flow-negative), Q3 2026 | Revenue $127.6B (+25%) vs. \~$128.2B; EPS $2.12 vs. \~$3.02 (an $8.7B investment loss cut $0.55); Cloud $30.7B (+103%), 36.2% margin | Backlog $561B (from $514B); capex $51.4B; 2026 guide held at $195B–$205B; 2027 to "rise significantly"; free cash flow −$9.1B | Down \~8–10% after hours; the July pattern repeated |
| Amazon (AMZN) | Reports Oct 29; AWS +37% to $42.2B last quarter; backlog $496B | Capex plan \~$220B; Q3 sales guide $197B–$202B | Largest implied move (±7.6%); Alphabet's drop raises the cash-flow bar |
| Meta (META, reported Oct 21) | Revenue +26% to $64.6B; free cash flow −$2.1B | 2026 capex now $135B–$145B | New non-voting class to fund AI shows how capital-hungry this is |
| Oracle, CoreWeave, Nebius | ORCL +10.7% Oct 28 on investor day: >35% yearly revenue growth FY26–FY30, ≥$225B FY30 revenue; CRWV +7.3%, NBIS +7.0% | Funding costs with the 10-year near 5%; CRWV bonds near 15% | The leveraged tail; moves 2–3x the hyperscalers on any news |

**Most likely to move:** Amazon on Oct 29, then CoreWeave and Nebius. Alphabet's drop shows cash burn now outweighs cloud growth for hyperscaler stocks, so AWS needs growth with capex its cash flow can carry. The neoclouds rallied on Oracle today but remain the most exposed to a December hike; CoreWeave is still \~30% below early September.

**Second-order effect:** Alphabet said TPU system sales were a meaningful part of Cloud growth and expects a bigger ramp in 2027, making Google a chip seller as well as a cloud. OpenAI and Oracle are reported to be using Google's chips. **Disclosure:** Anthropic, the company that makes me, is a large Google TPU customer, so weigh my framing here.

Sources: [247 Wall St (MSFT)](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/24/microsofts-50-billion-gamble-can-microsofts-azure-growth-justify-its-exploding-ai-budget/), [Fool (Google Cloud)](https://fool.com/investing/2026/10/11/alphabets-google-cloud-is-surging-at-82-and-the-he), [S&P Global (GOOGL)](https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/07/alphabet-postq-ai-growth-accelerates-as-spending-weighs-on-cash-flow), [GuruFocus (AMZN)](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8993599/), [Stockhub (META)](https://stockhub.kr/en/insights/view_1792615451713_r9j75cr7e), [Crypto Briefing (CRWV)](https://cryptobriefing.com/coreweave-shares-plunge-bond-yields-15/), [247 Wall St (CRWV)](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/20/coreweave-falls-4-as-hsbc-reiterates-bearish-call-on-debt-risk-nebius-drops-5-oracle-holds-steady/), [Tickzen (GOOGL preview)](https://tickzen.app/insights/alphabet-goog-q3-2026-earnings).

sections.title: AI infrastructure: power and cooling
sections.markdown:
The "picks and shovels" suppliers both reported blowout quarters this morning. They are the cleanest read on what hyperscaler capex turns into.

| Company | Q3 2026 result | What it tells us |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vertiv (VRT) | Sales $4.31B (+61%) vs. \~$3.75B expected; adj. EPS $2.21 vs. $1.82; organic orders up over 100%; raised full-year guidance | Power and cooling demand is accelerating, not peaking; stock was up \~4% early today |
| GE Vernova (GEV) | Orders $29B (+96% organic); backlog $197B; buyback raised to $20B | Gas turbines for data centers are sold out years ahead; expects 130+ GW under contract by year-end |
| SLB | Revenue $9.45B; highlighted Data Center Solutions as a separate growth driver | Even oil-services firms are selling into the AI power build |

**Most likely to move:** Vertiv, again. It rose \~16–17% on Oct 28 after its results, and Alphabet's signal of significantly higher 2027 capex supports the order book. But a one-day jump that size, plus Microsoft's $45.2B capex coming in below \~$50B, leaves room for profit-taking; Amazon's capex on Oct 29 is the next test. GE Vernova slipped \~1% and stays steadier, with a backlog contracted out to about 2031. ([StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/stock-market-today-live-october-28-2026), [RiskReversal](https://riskreversal.substack.com/p/fed-holds-msft-higher-googl-lower))

**Risk:** GE Vernova fell more than 14% in the month before earnings as investors worried about how AI gets financed. A capex pause from any hyperscaler hits this group fast.

Sources: [Vertiv Q3 release (TradingView)](https://www.tradingview.com/news/prnewswire:4c4865b67a1a7:0-vertiv-reports-strong-third-quarter-2026-with-net-sales-growth-of-61-organic-orders-growth-over-100-and-diluted-eps-growth-of-91-adjusted-diluted-eps-growth-of-78-raises-full-year-2026-guidance-across-all-key-metrics/), [MarketBeat (VRT)](https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/VRT/earnings/), [Yahoo (VRT)](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/VRT/), [GE Vernova 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001996810/000199681026000162/gevpressrelease3q26.htm), [247 Wall St (GEV)](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/24/the-ai-power-bill-comes-due-will-ge-vernovas-q3-earnings-oct-28-prove-its-176b-backlog-is-real/), [SLB release](https://www.benzinga.com/node/62553977).

sections.title: AI chips and memory
sections.markdown:
Memory got its strongest confirmation yet on Oct 28: SK Hynix posted record results and said DRAM and HBM are sold out through 2029. The chip index rose 1.8% (Micron +5.9%, Lam +5.4%, Applied +5.1%) while Nvidia fell 1.2%. Alphabet's 2027 capex signal and TPU ramp add demand; Microsoft's under-spend is the one soft spot. ([TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours))

| Company | Latest data point | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Micron (MU) | Says 2027 HBM is largely sold out at "much higher" prices; DRAM prices rose high-teens % last quarter, NAND \~30% | Every capex raise means more HBM orders; the shortage runs into 2028 by Micron's account |
| SK Hynix (SKHY, Nasdaq ADR) | Record Q3; says DRAM and HBM sold out through 2029; shares up \~13% on Oct 28 | Same thesis; TrendForce sees DRAM contract prices up another 10–15% in Q4 |
| TSMC (TSM) | Q3 revenue $46.7B, above the top of guidance; net income +68.7% | Strong but stock fell \~3% on margin dilution from 2 nm and U.S. fabs |
| Broadcom (AVGO) | Banks lining up a \~$63B financing to build AI compute (with Apollo, Blackstone) | Custom chips for AI labs, including Google's TPUs; Alphabet says TPU system sales ramp into 2027 |
| Intel (INTC) | Reports Oct 29; 30 upward EPS revisions in 30 days | Margin test after shares fell \~13% since July |
| AMD | Reports Nov 3; guided $12.7B–$13.3B | Data center sales expected to accelerate in H2 |
| Nvidia (NVDA) | Reports \~Nov 17–18; beat 7 of last 8 quarters | Sets the tone for the whole group |

**Most likely to move this week:** Micron and SK Hynix on pricing and capex, Broadcom on the TPU ramp, and Intel on its own report Oct 29 (implied ±9.4%). Nvidia faces a growing custom-chip story until its own report in mid-November.

**Risk:** Memory was the most crowded trade in the October selloff. SK Hynix fell 9.6% in one session during that slide, so the downside is just as sharp.

**Disclosure:** Some Broadcom financing reporting ties these deals to Anthropic, the company that makes me. I note it so you can weigh my framing.

Sources: [Tech Insider (Micron)](https://tech-insider.org/micron-ceo-2027-memory-supply-sold-out-2026/), [Computing for Geeks (TrendForce)](https://computingforgeeks.com/?p=175309), [Yahoo live blog](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-october-28-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-fed-meeting-decision-big-tech-earnings-130508769.html), [NordFX](https://nordfx.com/market-news/market-pulse-october-28-2026), [TSMC 6-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001046179/000104617926000726/a3q26e_withguidancexfinal.htm), [AllInvestView (TSMC)](https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/2330.TW/q3-2026/), [Yahoo (Broadcom)](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-october-28-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-fed-meeting-decision-big-tech-earnings-130508769.html), [247 Wall St (Intel)](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/25/intels-make-or-break-margin-test-is-arriving-on-oct-29/), [Benzinga (AMD)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/amd/earnings-forecasts), [The Right Trader (NVDA)](https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/nvda), [FX Leaders](https://www.fxleaders.com/?p=465067).

sections.title: AI software
sections.markdown:
ServiceNow's after-hours drop shows the AI-disruption trade against seat-based software is not over, even when growth and AI bookings beat. Companies selling AI outcomes still rerate up; legacy SaaS trades on fear that AI agents replace it.

| Company | Setup | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Palantir (PLTR) | Reports Nov 2; est. $0.36 EPS, $2.00B revenue; beat 5 straight quarters | Highest-multiple AI software name; guidance decides the reaction |
| ServiceNow (NOW) | Q3 subscription revenue $3.99B (+21%, +20.5% cc) vs. \~20% guide; AI contract-value target raised to $1.7B from $1B; EPS $1.00 vs. $1.02; Q4 guide below the Street; down \~14–16% after hours | Disruption fear won again despite beats on growth and AI |
| Microsoft (MSFT) | Copilot adoption and its own models, alongside Azure | The software side of tonight's report |
**Most likely to move:** Palantir on Nov 2 (implied ±12.0%). ServiceNow's reaction raises the bar: only accelerating growth with a strong guide is being rewarded. NOW's drop may also weigh on other seat-based software stocks at Thursday's open. ([Securities.io](https://www.securities.io/servicenow-q3-subscription-revenue-rises-21-to-3-988-million/), [PANews](https://panews.io/articles/01a1844b-23c0-762e-84fc-a5ee2a94208b))

**Sector event:** Anthropic has filed an S-1 to list on Nasdaq. A large AI listing can pull money from existing AI software stocks, or reprice them higher as a comparison point.

**Disclosure:** I'm built by Anthropic, so I'm not a neutral source on that IPO. I won't give a view on it; treat it purely as a sector catalyst.

Sources: [Benzinga (PLTR)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PLTR/earnings), [Earnings Whispers (PLTR drift)](https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/PLTR), [XTB (NOW)](https://www.xtb.com/cy/market-analysis/news-and-research/servicenow-shares-jump-7-after-earnings-is-the-software-sector-poised-for-a-rebound), [TIKR (NOW)](https://www.tikr.com/blog/servicenow-jumped-7-on-a-150-analyst-target-heres-where-the-stock-could-go), [Yahoo market wrap](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-news-oct-28-081900420.html).

sections.title: Oil and gas
sections.markdown:
Earnings are huge, but the stocks now trade on one binary question: does the Iran conflict end? A deal would cut the war premium quickly; refiners carry the most exposure.

| Company | Latest data point | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valero (VLO) | Q3 adj. EPS $23.90 vs. $20.30 expected; refining margin $39.24/bbl vs. $13.14 a year ago | Most leveraged to war-driven fuel margins, both ways |
| Exxon (XOM), Chevron (CVX) | Report Oct 30; Exxon flagged a $4.5B refining-margin boost; CVX est. $4.78 | Steadier; buybacks and Guyana/Permian growth cushion a price drop |
| SLB | Revenue $9.45B (+6%); Middle East up 13% sequentially despite disruption | Services lag the oil price; growing data center unit |

**Most likely to move:** Refiners (VLO, and Phillips 66 reporting about Nov 4). Iran's reply to the Qatari draft is due by week's end. President Trump has said he expects the war to end after the Nov 3 midterms, with oil falling. In August, the EIA forecast Brent at $69 in 2027 once Hormuz traffic normalizes.

**Upside case:** New supply shocks keep happening; a Saudi refinery was attacked this week and pushed oil higher.

Sources: [Oilprice (Valero)](https://oilprice.com/Company-News/Valero-Q3-Earnings-Surge-Sixfold-to-68-Billion-on-Refining-Boom.amp.html), [247 Wall St (Valero)](https://247wallst.com/cards/valero-energy-q3-2026-earnings-vlo-01m5hs2e7dnht5h4w2ey4hf68p), [Pluang (Exxon, Trump)](https://pluang.com/en/news-feed/trump-perkirakan-perang-iran-berakhir-harga-minyak-turun-setelah-pemilu), [SLB release](https://www.sttinfo.fi/tiedote/72439583/slb-announces-third-quarter-2026-results?publisherId=58763726), [AInvest (EIA)](https://www.ainvest.com/news/iran-oil-windfall-priced-eia-won-2608/), [investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/investinglive-european-fx-news-wrap-28-oct/), [Yahoo live blog](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-october-28-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-fed-meeting-decision-big-tech-earnings-130508769.html).

sections.title: Scenarios: what would change the picture
sections.markdown:
| If this happens | Likely winners | Likely losers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hyperscalers raise capex and cloud growth accelerates | MU, SKHY, VRT, GEV, AVGO, CRWV | Hyperscaler stocks themselves if cash flow weakens |
| Capex rises but cloud growth slows | Suppliers short-term | GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN (repeat of Alphabet's July drop) |
| Fed signals a December hike | Banks, cash | CRWV, NBIS, ORCL, high-multiple software |
| Fed sounds patient, yields ease below 5% | Leveraged AI builders, small caps | — |
| Iran deal reached | Airlines, consumers | VLO, XOM, CVX, oil services |
| Iran talks collapse | VLO, XOM, CVX | Rate-sensitive tech (oil feeds inflation, inflation feeds hikes) |

Oct 28 played out the "capex rises but the stock falls" row for Alphabet and the "Fed signals a December hike" row in muted form; Amazon on Oct 29 tests the first row again.
